lead: the first four months of a friendship are the whole of it. you find out everything there is inside three evenings, and then the finding-out is done and the friendship has eleven years left to run.
sun: a friendship here does not cool. it ends when the life does — the town, the work, the whole set of them, gone on one change of weather, with nobody dropped in particular and nothing said against anyone. one name crosses. it is never the one the old life would have chosen, either: it is whoever you owe something to, and that person gets rung from every address you have had since.
moon: the appetite is for finding somebody out, and it moves fast — two months into a new town you have people, real ones, because wanting to know somebody is a motive that shows on your face. it also completes. by the second year there is nothing further in there to find, and what carries the friendship from then on is upkeep, with the hunger already out ahead on somebody newer.
pull: every friend you have was made in the first season of a life, by somebody starving to know them, and each one has been kept since by somebody who already does.
tension: somewhere in the sixth year one of them asks, carefully, whether something has changed, because the questions stopped years ago and they noticed. nothing has changed. the friendship is as load-bearing as it was the spring you met, and the honest answer — that you finished finding them out in the first month and stayed on other grounds — lands as an insult in every version. so you say nothing has changed, and it settles nothing.
cost: a month is enough to be close to somebody, which most people take four years to do badly. the depth gets set that first season and does not increase, because nothing in you looks twice at the same person. and no friendship has survived a turn except the one that is owed — so the longest relationship in your life is with somebody you have no interest left in.

lead: the room was full when you did it — the thing came out at the size it was in you. you have been at everything they have held since, on time, and none of it gets mentioned.
sun: the season had closed weeks before the evening did. by the time you spoke there was nothing left in you to argue with, which is why it came out finished rather than furious — weather reported after the fact. what did not turn over was the people standing there. they are owed, one at a time, and none of that came off with the job or the version of you who held it.
moon: there is one setting here and it does not adjust for the occasion. so a thing you had finished quietly went into that room as an event: everyone present can still quote it, several of them wrongly, and it will be told at tables you are not sitting at for another twenty years. it went out whole. nothing that leaves at that size can be reissued smaller.
pull: the deciding took four months and the room got one minute of it. the minute is the entire record, and you have sat in that room every year since without amending a word.
tension: they filed it as temper, and the ones who filed it were present for the loud minute of a decision that took the winter before it. none of that winter was visible to anybody. and turning up every year since reads as somebody working their way toward an apology, so each year of attendance quietly buys another year of the version where you went off and are sorry.
cost: nothing you end goes through a whispering year first. no faction gets assembled, nobody is worked on quietly in advance, and the people it lands on hear it from you, in one piece, on the day. that day is then the most vivid thing about you in that room permanently. nine good years underneath it, and you are present while they are outranked by a minute.

lead: eleven years ago you ended it in one conversation and never wavered afterwards. last month your hand went toward her number with no sense of trespass, as though the silence had been weather rather than something you did.
sun: the finishing is done properly and it is done by you. no drift, no long fade, no stretch of being half in it — the season turns, whoever was in it is over, and every arrangement that person made gets closed out inside a fortnight. one thread is left standing, on purpose, and it is always a person. it is never any part of the thing itself.
moon: underneath, nothing files as gone. the one standing thread gets read as a general rule — that what leaves is out at the moment rather than over — so everything you have ended sits in you in working order, at the age it went, and none of it has ever been grieved. the reaching, when it comes, is innocent. it goes toward rooms you cleared yourself.
pull: you have finished nine things absolutely and grieved none of them. whatever would do the grieving never got the news, and holds all nine warm, waiting on a door you personally welded shut.
tension: the ending gets delivered in a voice that has not accepted it, so people go home believing something was left open. nothing was. they plan around a softness that exists only in the delivery, and learn a year later, from somebody else, that it was finished on the day. what they took for a change of mind was the wording, and the wording is the only part of you that ever hesitated.
cost: you can close a fifteen-year thing in an afternoon and eat normally that evening, and none of it is bravado. the loss is not cancelled, only unscheduled. it arrives a decade out, whole, at the moment your hand goes toward something you personally ended — and none of the nine has ever had a mourning arranged for it, so they come due at random, in supermarkets, decades late.

lead: the mourning was finished inside a season and the speed of it frightened people. nine years on, a good part of every week still goes to people you would not know at all except through him.
sun: the grief did not taper. it ran at full weight for one season and then the weather changed and it was over, properly over rather than buried, and you were working again inside a month — which several of them have not forgiven. what did not end with it is what he was owed. that stayed exactly where it was, with nobody alive to collect it, so it went to the people he left.
moon: the thing paying it out has no edges. so one debt to one dead man resolves, when you look, into nine living people who ring you — his sister, the two friends, the neighbour who found him — none of them ever formally taken on, none of them aware there is a list. nothing meters it. the total gets known when the last of the nine dies.
pull: the grief was over in a season. the feeding is nine years old and still going out to him, through nine other people, none of whom knows whose debt they are drawing on.
tension: the family reads all of it as somebody who never got over it, and says so kindly, and the reading is wrong at both ends: the getting-over was done inside four months, and the driving is not affection. putting that right would mean saying out loud that you have not missed him since the first year and will still be taking his sister to her appointments in twenty, and there is no room in which that sentence helps anyone.
cost: grief here actually completes, and completes early — no ten-year tail on it, no anniversary that takes a week out of you. the debt does not complete, because a debt is discharged by the one it is owed to, and the one it is owed to is dead. nine people go on drawing at a size no one has ever seen, on an account nobody living can call settled.
